 JUDGMENT

The petitioners No.1 to 3, have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Smt.Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma., who died in a motor vehicle accident said to have occurred on 29.06.2022.

The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 29.06.2022 at about 7.15 p.m., the deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamm was proceeding in a Tata Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098 along with her house hold goods, the same was driven by its driver from Mohan Lodge towards Panigava village on Ram Mandir Ring Road in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations,
reached near old Chavargi road railway underpass, due to his negligence driving lost control over the vehicle and dashed to iron bar poles.
Due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Sunrise Hospital, Kalaburgi wherein the deceased took treatment as inpatient, then for further treatment referred to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru SCCH4 4 MVC No.6905/2022 wherein the deceased took treatment as an inpatient wherein the deceased succumbed to the fatal injuries and died on 30.07.2022 and post mortem was conducted in the same hospital and the petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards the hospitalization, nourishment, conveyance, transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
4.

Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was very hale and healthy and she was working as Teacher in Private School and she was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month and out of his entire income was contributed and maintaining the family members.
Due to untimely death of deceased in the traffic accident, the petitioners have been put to great financial hardship and untold misery and depressed.
SCCH4 5 MVC No.6905/2022

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 and 2 are owner and insurer of the offending Tata Eicher goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA31AA1098 and they are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ with interest.
7. After service of notices the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and filed their separate written statements.

8. The respondent No.1, in his written statement has admitted that he is the RC owner of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098 and it has insured with respondent No.2, the policy was in force as on the date of SCCH4 6 MVC No.6905/2022 the accident.
The said accident was occurred only due to the negligence of the deceased person.
9. The respondent No.2, in the written statement has contended that respondent No.1 prove the existence of the policy by producing the original policy before this court.
The respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle driven the vehicle without having the driving license.
There is no fitness certificate and permit to the vehicle of the respondent No.1 ply the vehicle on the road at the material time of the accident.
There is in ordinate delay in lodging the complaint for the period of one day the accident was took place on 29.06.2022 and complaint was lodged on 30.06.2022.
The deceased was negligently going as a gratuitous passenger in the vehicle of the respondent No.1 and he himself negligently fall from the vehicle and contributed the accident.

The respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle allowed unauthorized SCCH4 7 MVC No.6905/2022 passengers to travel in the vehicle at the material time of accident, knowing fully well that it is not permitted.
10. Further both respondents have denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 have prays to dismiss the petition.

11. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed :
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma died in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 29.06.2022 at about 7.15 p.m., on Mohan Lodge to Ram Manadir Ring Road, near Railway Under Bridge, Kalaburgi due to the rash and negligence driving of the TATA ACE Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced certified copies of FIR, statement of my brother Chethan Given to the police, charge sheet, spot mahazar, IMV report, Inquest report, PM report and death certificate which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 8.
16.
As per the documents deceased Chethan has lodged complaint with Kalaburagi Traffic Police on 30.06.2022.

As per the complaint it has been alleged that, on 29.06.2022, at 7.15 PM, the complainant and deceased were looking after complainant's father in doctor Vishwanatha Patil Hospital complainant's mother Laxmi in order to bring meals from Panigava village she went in TATA Ace Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098 driven by Dharmasingh.

After some times the complainant received a phone call from Yallalinga and he toled that while he was along with Gundappa, their SCCH4 10 MVC No.6905/2022 villager Darmasingh, near the railway bridge, Jevargi, drove the the TATA Ace goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA 32AA1098 in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to Iron bar poles, the said accident, the complainant mother Laxmi sustained injury and she was admitted to Sunrise Hospital hospital.

17. On the basis of complaint the police have registered FIR against Dharmasingh, the driver of the goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098, thereafter, the police have visited the place of the accident and drawn spot mahazar.
Since the injured Laxmi died, PM reexport is done on 30.07.2022.
In the PM report it is noted that, the injured Laxmi died due to respiratory failure, as a Naveen Kumar vs Dharam Singh on 15 February, 2024

. The police have also conducted inquest.
The injuries found on the dead body of the Laxmi are noted in the PM report as well as Inquest report.
The petitioner has also SCCH4 11 MVC No.6905/2022 produced the death certificate of the deceased Venkatalakshmamma.
18. The jurisdictional police, after completion of the investigation have laid charge sheet against respondent No.1/Dharmasingh, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304 (A) of IPC.
The allegation made in the charge sheet as well as complaint are one and the same.

19. The respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.1, and got marked his driving license,
insurance policy and RC card are marked at Ex.R.1 to 3.

In written statement as well as examinationinchief it is the contention of the 1st respondent that there is no his negligence but the accident was occurred to due the negligence of the deceased person.
That means the respondent do not dispute the accident and death of Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma in the said accident.

The respondent No.2 has examined its official namely Pradeep as RW.2, through him authorization letter to give evidence and insurance policy which are marked at Ex.4 and 5.
21.
It is the main defence of the respondent No.2 that, the vehicle of the respondent No.1 is absolutely meant for carrying goods except driver no person is entitled to go in the vehicle.
The respondent No.1 owner of the vehicle allowed the unauthorized passengers to travel in the vehicle at the material time of accident, knowing fully well that it is not permitted to respondent No.1.
the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.
So this respondent also do not dispute the accident and death of Laxmi @ Venkatalaxmi in the said accident.
22. In the claim petition like the present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities SCCH4 13 MVC No.6905/2022 is sufficient.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, the deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma died due to the accidental injuries sustained to her while she was traveling in the vehicle the goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA32AA1098,driven by the 1st respondent who is also the owner of the same and the said accident was occurred due to negligence of the 1st respondent.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:

As per these documents the petitioner No.1 and 2 are the the sons and petitioner No.3 is the motherinlaw of the deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma.,.
These documents are not disputed by the respondents.

In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners is to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners being SCCH4 15 MVC No.6905/2022 the sons and motherinlaw of the deceased, are the dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
25.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.

In this regard the petitioners have produced aadhar card of the deceased marked at Ex.P.10 wherein the date of birth of the year deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma., mentioned as 1975 the accident was occurred on 29.06.2022.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 47 years.
26. As stated in the petition the deceased was working as Teacher in Private School and she was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ per month.
In this regard the petitioners have not produced any documents.

In the absence of proof of income the notional income of the SCCH4 16 MVC No.6905/2022 deceased was Rs.15,500/ in the year2022, then the annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/.
27.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is '13'.
The future loss of income is Rs.24,18,000/.

Since the deceased left his sons and motherinlaw, it is considered that, there are three dependents of deceased, hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.16,12,000/ (Rs. 15,500/ X 12 X 13= Rs.24,18,000/ minus 1/3rd = Rs.8,06,000/).

28. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the SCCH4 17 MVC No.6905/2022 established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

29. In another reported decision in Civil Appeal Nos.1920 of 2021 in between Kirti and Another etc., V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., as follows;
"When it comes to the second category of cases, relating to notional income for non earning victims, it is my opinion that the above principle applies with equal vigor,

sentences.text: Once notional income is determined, the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do SCCH4 18 MVC No.6905/2022 not take place in the domain of work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant,J., in his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654:
Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)".
30.

As per the above decision, 25% of notional income should be added to total loss of dependency,
to the age of deceased, which will be Rs.4,03,000/
Further the petitioners have also produced medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.4,33,139/.
This medical bills are not disproved.
So petitioner is entitled for the same.

The petitioners No.1 to 3, hence I inclined to award a sum of Rs.44,000/ for loss of consortium,
Rs.27,500/ towards loss of love and affection, Rs.16,500/ towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/
towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

32. The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads;
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 16,12,000/
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 4,03,000/
3. Loss of consortium to the Rs. 44,000/ petitioners 4. Loss of love and affection to the Rs. 27,500/ petitioners 5.

Loss of estate Rs. 16,500/
6.

Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/
7.
Medical expenses Rs. 4,33,139/ Total Rs. 25,52,639/ SCCH4 20 MVC No.6905/2022 33.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
But the respondent No.2 has taken up a defence that they are not liable to pay the compensation, since the deceased was travailing as a gratuitous passenger in the inured vehicle.

sentences.text: In the complaint lodged by the son of the deceased Laxmi it has been specifically mentioned that, the said Laxmi was going in the vehicle of the respondent No.1 to bring meals to the hospital where her husband was admitted.
The same allegation also made in the charge sheet.

35. In the written statement as well as examination in chief of RW.1 also it is not stated that, the deceased was shifting the house hold articles but only in the claim petition it has been stated that,
the deceased Laxmi @ Venkatalakshmamma was shifting her house hold articles in the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1.

If at all the respondent No.1 was shifting house hold SCCH4 21 MVC No.6905/2022 articles belonging to the deceased her son who has lodged complaint with the police would have mentioned in the same in the complaint.

36. There is no acceptable evidence to prove that, the deceased was shifting the house hold articles in the vehicle belonging to the respondent No.1, as such it is not possible to believe that, the deceased was belonging to her house hold articles.

37. The 1st respondent only in the cross examination has deposed that, deceased was sifting her house hold articles, in the lorry of 1st respondent, hence she was traveling in the lorry as owner of the house hold article, traveling in the 1st respondent's vehicle.
All the police records shows that deceased was going in the vehicle of 1st respondent from hospital to bring meals.
This statement is not supported with documentary evidence.
It appears that RW.1, just to avoid the SCCH4 22 MVC No.6905/2022 responsibility of his owner/1st respondent, has stated deceased was traveling with house hold article.
The version of RW.1 is not acceptable under law.
The petitioner by admitting contents of one part of the charge sheet, can't deny other part of the same.

38. In National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bommithi Subbhayamma (2005) 12 SCC 243 in which the Supreme Court has laid down that the Insurance Company is not liable for payment of any compensation for death of a gratuitous passenger traveling in a goods vehicle.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bommithi Subbhayamma (2005) 12 SCC 243
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble supreme court in catena of decisions.
In view of the above citation liability can't be saddled on the respondent No.2.
The respondent No.1 being owner of the offending vehicle shall pay compensation to the petitioners interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the SCCH4 23 MVC No.6905/2022 affirmative.

39.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.25,52,639/
(Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Six Hundred and Thirty Nine Only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,.

8 from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:40:20.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1 and 2, 50% shall be released to petitioner No.1 and 2 on their proper identification and remaining 50% shall be SCCH4 24 MVC No.6905/2022 kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.3, it is ordered to release the entire amount in her favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/.
Draw the award accordingly.
